_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for the Republic of the Congo (Congo-Brazzaville) covering early Bantu settlement, Kongo Kingdom, Teke Kingdom, French Congo and French Equatorial Africa, Congo-Ocean Railway forced labour, independence, Marxist period, Sassou-Nguesso, civil wars, and oil economy.

ethnic_groups.name: Kongo
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; Lari, Vili, Sundi subgroups; southern Congo; Pool region; civil war militia base

ethnic_groups.name: Téké
ethnic_groups.notes: Central plateaux; historical Teke/Tio Kingdom; Makoko treaty with de Brazza

ethnic_groups.name: Mbochi
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Congo; Sassou-Nguesso's ethnic base; Cuvette region

ethnic_groups.name: Pygmy (BaAka, BaMbenzele)
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous forest hunter-gatherers in northern rainforests; marginalised

ethnic_groups.name: Vili
ethnic_groups.notes: Coastal Kongo subgroup; Pointe-Noire area; Loango Kingdom heritage

current_leader.name: Denis Sassou-Nguesso
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Also served 1979-1992; returned to power by force during civil war; total 40+ years in power

former_presidents.name: Fulbert Youlou
former_presidents.notes: Abbé Youlou; first president; ousted by Trois Glorieuses popular uprising

former_presidents.name: Joachim Yhombi-Opango
former_presidents.notes: Brief military rule; later opposition figure

former_presidents.name: Pascal Lissouba
former_presidents.notes: Democratically elected; ousted in civil war; died in exile 2020

910.name: Early Bantu Settlement and Iron Age
910.description: Bantu-speaking peoples migrate into the Congo Basin; ironworking and agriculture replace hunter-gatherer economies; BaTwa (Pygmy) peoples remain in the forests.

sub_clusters.name: Bantu Migration into the Congo Basin
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking farmers from the Cameroon-Nigeria borderland migrate southward and eastward through the equatorial forest; yam and oil-palm cultivation.

sub_clusters.name: Iron Age Communities
sub_clusters.description: Iron smelting sites in the Niari Valley and Pool Malebo region; development of trade networks along the Congo River system.

920.name: Kongo Kingdom (Northern Territories)
920.description: The Kongo Kingdom's northern provinces extend into modern Congo-Brazzaville; trade, Christianity, and political organisation shape the region.

sub_clusters.name: Kongo Northern Provinces
sub_clusters.description: Provinces of Nsundi and Mpangu extend Kongo influence north of the Congo River; trade in copper, raffia cloth, and nzimbu shells.

sub_clusters.name: Kongo Christianity and Portuguese Contact
sub_clusters.description: Kongo Kingdom adopts Christianity after Portuguese contact 1491; Afonso I's Christian kingdom; syncretic religious practices spread northward.

920.name: Teke (Tio) Kingdom
920.description: The Teke Kingdom controls trade at Pool Malebo (Stanley Pool); mediates between coast and interior; the Makoko's authority shapes the region.

sub_clusters.name: Teke Control of Pool Malebo Trade
sub_clusters.description: Teke (Tio/Anziku) kingdom controls strategic Pool Malebo portage; monopolises ivory and slave trade between coast and upper Congo.

sub_clusters.name: Loango Kingdom and Coastal Trade
sub_clusters.description: Loango Kingdom on the Atlantic coast (Pointe-Noire region); independent of Kongo; major slave-trading port; Dutch and French commerce.

930.name: Atlantic Slave Trade and Coastal Commerce
930.description: The Loango coast becomes a major slave-exporting region; internal wars fuel captive supply; European factories dot the littoral.

sub_clusters.name: Loango Coast Slave Trade
sub_clusters.description: Loango, Malemba, and Cabinda ports export hundreds of thousands of enslaved people; Dutch, French, and Portuguese traders compete; trade transforms local societies.

sub_clusters.name: Pierre de Brazza and the Makoko Treaty
sub_clusters.description: Italian-French explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza signs a treaty with Teke king Makoko Iloo I 1880; establishes French claim to the north bank of the Congo.

940.name: French Congo and AEF (1882–1960)
940.description: Brazzaville becomes capital of French Equatorial Africa; concessionary companies, forced labour, and the deadly Congo-Ocean Railway construction.

sub_clusters.name: Concessionary Companies and Exploitation
sub_clusters.description: Vast concessions granted to private companies for rubber and ivory; André Gide's Voyage au Congo (1927) exposes abuses; international scandal.

sub_clusters.name: Congo-Ocean Railway (CFCO)
sub_clusters.description: Construction of the Congo-Océan railway from Brazzaville to Pointe-Noire; estimated 17,000–23,000 forced labourers die; one of colonial Africa's worst atrocities.

sub_clusters.name: Brazzaville Conference 1944
sub_clusters.description: De Gaulle's Brazzaville Conference (January–February 1944) promises post-war reforms for French Africa but explicitly excludes independence.

950.name: Independence and Early Republic
950.description: Fulbert Youlou leads independence; overthrown by trade unions 1963; Massamba-Débat introduces African socialism.

sub_clusters.name: Abbé Youlou and Independence
sub_clusters.description: Abbé Fulbert Youlou becomes first president; Congo independent 15 August 1960; authoritarian rule; 'Trois Glorieuses' uprising topples him 1963.

sub_clusters.name: Massamba-Débat and African Socialism
sub_clusters.description: Alphonse Massamba-Débat introduces MNR single-party socialism; youth militia; relations with Cuba and China; ousted by military 1968.

950.name: Marxist-Leninist People's Republic
950.description: Marien Ngouabi declares People's Republic of Congo; PCT (Parti Congolais du Travail) Marxist-Leninist one-party state; assassinations and coups.

sub_clusters.name: Ngouabi and the PCT
sub_clusters.description: Captain Marien Ngouabi establishes Marxist-Leninist state; renames country People's Republic of Congo; assassinated March 1977.

sub_clusters.name: Sassou-Nguesso First Term
sub_clusters.description: Denis Sassou-Nguesso takes power 1979; maintains Marxist label but cultivates French and oil company ties; agrees to multiparty transition 1991.

960.name: Democratic Transition and Civil Wars
960.description: National conference; Lissouba elected 1992; militia-based civil wars (1993, 1997, 1998–99); Sassou-Nguesso returns to power by force.

sub_clusters.name: Lissouba Presidency and Political Crisis
sub_clusters.description: Pascal Lissouba wins multiparty election 1992; ethnic militias (Cocoyes, Cobras, Ninjas) form; political violence escalates.

sub_clusters.name: Civil Wars (1997–1999)
sub_clusters.description: Sassou-Nguesso's Cobra militia and Angolan forces seize Brazzaville June–October 1997; second war 1998–99 devastates Pool region; tens of thousands killed.

960.name: Sassou-Nguesso and the Petro-State
960.description: Sassou-Nguesso consolidates authoritarian rule; oil revenues fund patronage; constitutional amendments; international corruption investigations.

sub_clusters.name: Sassou-Nguesso's Authoritarian Consolidation
sub_clusters.description: Post-war reconstruction; new constitution 2002; Pool region pacification; opposition marginalised; term limit removed 2015 via referendum.

sub_clusters.name: Oil Economy and Corruption
sub_clusters.description: Congo becomes sub-Saharan Africa's third-largest oil producer; oil funds presidential patronage; 'biens mal acquis' French corruption investigations target Sassou family.

sub_clusters.name: Pool Region Ninja Insurgency
sub_clusters.description: Pastor Ntumi's Ninja militia controls parts of Pool region for years; periodic clashes; ceasefire 2017; region remains marginalised.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
